launches.title: Grok releases the first seven minutes of its AI-generated ‘Odyssey’
launches.excerpt: Grok has released the first seven minutes of its artificial intelligence-generated adaptation of The Odyssey, titled Episode 1 of the Odyssey series. The project was created three months after Elon Musk announced plans for the film, developed in collaboration with Wonder Studios and director Dev Walker. Musk had previously criticised Christopher Nolan’s cinematic version of the epic for casting nonwhite and transgender actors. While Nolan’s film relied heavily on practical filmmaking across six countries and became a major box office success, the Grok adaptation was produced using artificial intelligence tools. The released footage features characters with Musk-approved skin tones and a narrator with a British accent, while the characters speak English rather than ancient Greek. Reviewers note that although individual visual shots can appear realistic, the overall production lacks artistic inspiration, momentum, and engaging dialogue. The clip consists largely of exposition and bearded characters delivering stilted lines. Maintaining attention throughout the seven-minute runtime proved challenging compared to longer, traditional feature films. Further releases from the project remain planned, though critical reception indicates limited enthusiasm for a full-length version.

launches.title: Rocket Report: SpaceX says no thanks to military launches; Spanish rocket nearly ready
launches.excerpt: SpaceX recently declined three military launch contracts offered by the US Space Force, which were left unfilled as other providers manage existing backlogs. Meanwhile, a NASA safety panel estimated that up to 22 refuelings may be required for a SpaceX Starship lunar landing, though Elon Musk disputed this figure by suggesting a range of six to eight flights instead. SpaceX is now targeting November for its fifteenth Starship test flight, during which the company plans to attempt catches of both the Super Heavy first stage and the upper stage. In other launch news, PLD Space is preparing its Miura 5 small-lift rocket for an inaugural flight before mid-2027. Canadian startup Reaction Dynamics is seeking funding to develop its Aurora and Borealis rockets, while Rocket Lab is preparing for its 98th Electron mission. Japan successfully launched its Martian Moons eXploration mission aboard an upgraded H3 rocket, and debris from a September Chinese rocket launch was recently discovered in Minnesota. Additionally, Arianespace scheduled its next Ariane 6 flight for late November following a turbopump investigation. Blue Origin announced a major expansion of its Florida facilities to support increased flight rates for the New Glenn rocket, including additional launch pads and manufacturing capabilities.

launches.title: Amazon MWAA now available in Mexico (Central) Region
launches.excerpt: Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow Provisioned environments have expanded to include the Mexico Central Region, designated as mx-central-1. While Amazon MWAA Serverless was previously accessible in this specific Region, local users can now utilise Provisioned environments for running their Apache Airflow workflows. Amazon MWAA functions as a managed orchestration service designed to simplify the setup and operation of large-scale, end-to-end data pipelines within the cloud. Users are able to establish these new Provisioned environments through several standard deployment interfaces, including the AWS Management Console, the AWS CLI, the AWS SDKs, and AWS CloudFormation. By deploying these workflows in the Mexico Central Region, organisations can operate them in closer physical proximity to their primary data sources and end users. This geographical alignment serves to minimise operational latency and assists businesses in complying with local data residency requirements. Further information regarding these capabilities and availability can be found directly on the official Amazon MWAA product page and the corresponding supported Regions documentation.

launches.title: Amazon EMR on EKS reduces EMR charge by 30 percent
launches.excerpt: Amazon has announced a thirty percent reduction in the EMR charge that is added to EKS when running EMR on EKS. This price decrease affects both the per-vCPU-hour charge and the per-GB-hour charge associated with the service. Meanwhile, the underlying Amazon EKS charges will remain completely unchanged from their previous rates. All EMR workloads that are currently running on the EKS deployment option will benefit directly from this pricing change. Customers can now run Apache Spark workloads on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service at a notably lower cost. The new pricing structure applies automatically to all existing EMR on EKS workloads without requiring any additional action from users. This thirty percent price reduction is available across all AWS Regions where Amazon EMR on EKS is currently supported. Users who wish to learn more about the update can visit the official Amazon EMR on EKS documentation and the Amazon EMR pricing page.

launches.title: Latest estimate for Starship launches required to support a Moon landing? 22.
launches.excerpt: NASA has historically been reluctant to disclose the exact number of Starship launches required to fuel a lunar lander in low-Earth orbit for the Artemis programme. Previous estimates provided by agency officials have ranged from the high single digits and low double digits to the high teens. During a quarterly meeting of the NASA Aerospace Safety Advisory Panel, panel member Charlie Precourt stated that the latest estimate is approximately 22 flights. Although Precourt did not explicitly name the vehicle, the figure solely applies to SpaceX's Starship, as Blue Origin's lunar lander does not rely on orbital refueling for its initial mission design. Following the public disclosure of the 22-flight estimate, SpaceX founder Elon Musk disputed the figure on social media, describing it as inaccurate and stating that the actual requirement would be closer to six to eight launches. Uncertainty remains regarding cryogenic propellant boil-off in orbit and the efficiency of transferring liquid oxygen and methane between spacecraft. Achieving the necessary refueling schedule presents a significant logistical challenge, even if SpaceX manages to increase its launch frequency in the coming years. Precourt noted that the situation poses risks to the mission success and schedule of Artemis IV, while praising agency leadership for assisting developers to overcome developmental barriers. NASA is currently working toward achieving a human lunar landing by 2028.

geo.title: Brazil runoff live updates: world leaders congratulate Lula on historic election win as Bolsonaro refuses to concede
geo.excerpt: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won Brazil’s presidential runoff election, defeating his far-right opponent Flávio Bolsonaro to claim a historic fourth term in power. According to Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court, Lula secured 51.79 percent of the vote, translating to approximately 4.4 million more votes than Bolsonaro, who finished with 48.21 percent. Flávio Bolsonaro, a senator and the eldest son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, has refused to accept the result and called for the election to be annulled. He specifically questioned a late-Sunday decision by a supreme court justice that extended voting by two hours due to alleged voter transport irregularities. This refusal to concede mirrors his father's actions after losing the 2022 presidential election to Lula. Lula’s victory makes him the first president in Brazilian history to secure a fourth term. It also marks the first time since Brazil’s return to democracy in 1988 that a candidate who trailed in the first round of voting successfully overturned the result in a runoff. Lula is scheduled to begin his new presidential term on 5 January 2027. Numerous world leaders have offered their congratulations to Lula following his victory, while the United States president has not yet issued a public response.

geo.title: Crowds welcome Venezuela's María Machado after months in exile
geo.excerpt: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado has returned to her home country after spending more than ten months in exile. Her arrival followed several previous unsuccessful attempts to re-enter Venezuela. Machado announced her return on Sunday in a post on X, stating that she was there with the people. Following her return, she attended a church service in the state of Lara, where she was surrounded by enthusiastic supporters. Large crowds subsequently gathered along the route of her journey through the capital city of Caracas. Her return follows significant political upheaval in the country, beginning when the United States seized her political opponent, President Nicolás Maduro, in January. That event occurred one month after Machado had fled Venezuela under cover of darkness in order to travel to Norway to accept the Nobel Peace Prize. Following Maduro's removal, the administration of US President Donald Trump supported his deputy, Delcy Rodríguez, as leader. Rodríguez was subsequently sworn in as the interim president of Venezuela.

geo.title: Thousands greet opposition leader Maria Machado upon return to Caracas
geo.excerpt: Thousands of supporters lined the streets of Venezuela’s capital Caracas to welcome opposition leader Maria Corina Machado home following a period of ten months in exile. Machado had fled the South American country in December of the previous year. Her departure occurred shortly before the United States abducted President Nicolas Maduro. Following Maduro's removal, the US administration backed his deputy, Delcy Rodriguez, to take over as the nation's leader. The large crowds gathered to greet Machado as she returned to the capital city. The event marked a significant public appearance for the opposition figure since her self-imposed exile abroad. Security presence was notable as citizens turned out in large numbers along the thoroughfares of Caracas. Machado's return highlights ongoing political developments in Venezuela following the leadership transition led by Rodriguez. Observers and supporters alike monitored her arrival closely amidst the current national context.

geo.title: Palestinians are opening their doors to the displaced of besieged Hebron
geo.excerpt: Israeli forces have demolished a three-storey building and industrial facilities in the Farsh Al-Hawa area of Hebron in the occupied West Bank, following an attack by two Palestinians on a military checkpoint that killed two soldiers and injured others. Israel’s Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich confirmed he ordered the destructions as part of a sweeping military assault on the city, which has been placed under lockdown. The operation has forcibly displaced more than 2,000 Palestinians, nearly half of whom are children and babies, alongside pregnant women and elderly residents. In response to the crisis, Palestinian authorities have declared a state of emergency and formed a crisis group involving government agencies, civil society and the private sector. Local residents and philanthropists, including real estate developer Mohamed Al-Rujoob, have opened their homes and properties to shelter displaced families. The military lockdown affects nearly one million people across Hebron and its district, restricting movement and forcing schools and universities to transition to online learning. The Fawwar refugee camp has also been sealed off by Israeli soldiers, preventing residents from entering or leaving the area. Many residents believe the military campaign is politically motivated ahead of Tuesday's general election, with right-wing ministers in Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition vying for votes.

invest.title: Marc Lore’s Wonder bets on Texas, automation and user-built restaurants as it mulls IPO
invest.excerpt: Food startup Wonder operates as a vertically integrated food technology platform offering takeout and delivery from multiple restaurant concepts under one roof. Founded in 2018 by Marc Lore, the company has raised 3.3 billion dollars from investors and achieved a valuation of 9 billion dollars during its latest funding round. Wonder currently operates 170 storefronts across several states and plans to expand into Texas next year with a target of at least 100 locations by the end of 2027. The company utilizes commissary kitchens for food preparation, while individual locations finish the menu items in all-electric spaces designed to reduce renovation costs. Wonder also owns Grubhub, which allows customers ordering through the startup app to avoid delivery fees and inflated menu prices. The firm plans to introduce a subscription program named Wonder Create, enabling users to establish their own virtual restaurants using artificial intelligence tools. Additionally, the business is developing an artificial intelligence platform called MEL to create personalised meal plans based on health data. Wonder is preparing for a potential initial public offering, having hired a chief financial officer earlier in the year, although the exact timing remains unconfirmed. While the company has secured high customer retention rates in competitive markets, it has operated at a financial loss following major acquisitions and faces ongoing scrutiny regarding food quality and pricing from some consumers.

invest.title: Neocloud stocks fall as Elon Musk says more than 200 of them face 'guppy-level death'
invest.excerpt: Shares of major neocloud companies fell in premarket trading on Monday following a social media post by Elon Musk warning that more than 200 firms in the sector face potential collapse and consolidation. Nebius, CoreWeave and Iren initially dropped more than 4 percent before paring some of their losses. Musk stated on X that debt markets have nearly shut off funding for companies lacking substantial revenue independent of artificial intelligence data centres, predicting widespread failures. SpaceX, led by Musk, operates its own data centres and competes directly with these neocloud providers that rent out computing capacity. The warning followed a post by investor Chamath Palihapitiya, who predicted a turbulent period in 2027 featuring stranded compute inventory and poor returns on bad bets. Neocloud stocks have experienced significant declines over the past month, with CoreWeave, Nebius and Iren falling by 30 to 40 percent amid investor anxiety over heavy borrowing to purchase expensive Nvidia chips and build infrastructure. Despite these concerns, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang defended the sector during an interview in Berlin, stating that demand for neoclouds is extremely high and that capital shortages will be resolved. Executives from Nebius and Iren also defended their financial positions and customer demand, noting that they anticipate selling out upcoming capacity.

invest.title: Cracking AI trade has Wall Street looking for a hedge. An ex-Citadel quant may have the answer
invest.excerpt: As financial markets grapple with declining shares in companies like CoreWeave, investors are increasingly searching for methods to hedge against potential drops in artificial intelligence demand. Former Citadel Securities quantitative researcher Jasper Zhang is addressing this challenge through Hyperbolic, a fifty-person financial technology startup he leads. The company is developing a spot marketplace for tradable graphics processing unit computing power, using software that virtually connects mismatched hardware clusters globally to create standardized units. This system aims to give traders control over underlying GPUs and serve as a foundation for physically settled GPU futures. Because GPU architecture, networking, memory, and security vary widely across data centres, traditional survey-based indices struggle to capture accurate setup costs. Hyperbolic intends to eliminate this basis risk by allowing investors to trade the hardware itself rather than relying solely on financial settlements. Since launching in 2022, the startup has raised twenty million dollars, is pursuing an additional funding round, and reports roughly 250,000 users alongside two hundred million dollars in connected annual GPU compute. Meanwhile, other major industry players are pursuing alternative hedging instruments, such as cash-settled futures products currently proposed by CME Group and backed by index providers like Silicon Data. However, executives at Hyperbolic argue that cash-settled derivatives fail to reflect real-world usage or put idle hardware to work during a market slowdown. By connecting users directly to physical infrastructure, the platform aims to provide a practical pipeline for smaller startups and help mitigate debt risks for data centre operators.
